decisive_join: Recover the operative Local Law 144 transaction and distinguish its group audit, notice, data, auditor, and deployer burdens from an individual false-negative or substantive-validity finding.

findings.claim: New York City currently imposes an operative audit, public-summary, and notice transaction on covered AEDT use.
limits: Coverage turns on the actual tool and deployment; this wave does not classify a named system.

findings.claim: The recovered implementation law distinguishes auditor independence, permissible data, publication, and notice rather than treating a vendor assurance as sufficient.
limits: DCWP does not certify an auditor roster, and the record does not adjudicate any audit's adequacy.

findings.claim: The employer or employment agency retains the compliance burden even when a vendor supplies the tool or audit materials.
limits: This does not decide contractual allocation or liability in a specific case.

findings.claim: Local Law 144 supplies group-impact transparency but not an individual false-negative rate, a complete disability accommodation ruling, or proof of job-related validity.
limits: A separate role, construct, accommodation, human-review, and outcome record is required.

observations.notes: A covered AEDT is a computational process derived from machine learning, statistical modeling, data analytics, or artificial intelligence that substantially assists or replaces discretionary employment decision-making.
observations.subject: NYC automated employment decision tool

observations.notes: Use requires a bias audit conducted no more than one year before use and a publicly available summary.
observations.subject: Covered AEDT use

observations.notes: Candidates or employees receive notice at least ten business days before use, including the job qualifications or characteristics being evaluated.
observations.subject: NYC candidate or employee

observations.notes: The transaction includes data-source and retention disclosure plus instructions for requesting an alternative selection process or accommodation.
observations.subject: AEDT notice and request process

observations.notes: The FAQ defines minimum auditor independence and leaves ultimate compliance responsibility with the employer or employment agency rather than the vendor.
observations.subject: NYC AEDT audit

observations.notes: The audit is a group selection-rate audit; it does not observe rejected individuals' counterfactual performance or prove the tool's substantive validity for the role.
observations.subject: Individual rejected candidate and role validity

selection_rule: Treat the enacted law and adopted rule as authority; use DCWP FAQs and CCHR guidance to clarify implementation while preserving tool classification, audit sufficiency, disability facts, and individual outcomes as open.

prohibited_inferences: every hiring technology is an AEDT
a published audit proves substantive validity
a vendor bears the employer's statutory burden
the law requires every alternative process request to be granted
group selection rates identify individual counterfactual success

title: New York City AEDT audit, notice, and deployer responsibility
